clue.text: Instigate frolic in gym

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word's letters go inside the second's

blocks.note: PT, physical training, is school gym
to romp is to frolic

explanation.surface: Someone starts horseplay in the school gym.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the old British school name for gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt something is to set it going or provoke it, a straightforward synonym of instigate.

clue.text: Redevelopment in old town starts civil disorder

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is used

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a historic town centre sparks unrest among residents.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance, the standard name for an outbreak of civil disorder.

clue.text: Spread out Parmesan, lacking an inferior cheese

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the next words are removed from the cheese name
spread is read as a verb telling us to scatter and lay out the letters anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the Italian hard cheese
taken as written; these two letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Instructions for spreading out some Parmesan, while dismissing another cheese as second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is part of the letters to rearrange. Remove AN from PARMESAN, then rearrange OUT + PARMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is a jokey British name for cheap, poor-quality cheddar, the sort only fit for baiting traps.

clue.text: Go round tree that's meretricious

indicators.note: one word going round another means it wraps around it

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk round a tree that happens to be gaudy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' looks like a walking instruction, but 'Go' is a noun meaning an attempt, and it wraps the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Meretricious means showily attractive but cheap and tasteless, which is what something trashy is.

clue.text: Chosen people get odd mixture of gold and silver

blocks.note: the elect are those chosen, especially by God
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: The chosen ones are handed a peculiar blend of precious metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like an anagram signal for what follows, but it is simply RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrum is a natural or man-made alloy of these two precious metals, used for early coins.

clue.text: Evangelism after presenting a form of immortality

indicators.note: giving a form of something means reshaping it into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Preaching the gospel is offered as a route to eternal life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a positional instruction but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting renown that never dies is a kind of immortality, living on in memory rather than in body.

clue.text: Compulsory measure for about a month

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the month's abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
taken as written
Dec is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: A rule is imposed as mandatory for a period of about a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About a month' reads like a duration of roughly four weeks; 'about' actually turns the month's abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enforced is imposed and required by authority, so it is obligatory rather than optional.

clue.text: Deal with entertainment paid for by another

blocks.note: first meaning: to handle or behave towards
second meaning: a meal or outing someone else pays for

explanation.surface: Handling an outing that someone else is funding.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means handle or act towards; as a noun it is something enjoyable that a host pays for.

clue.text: Release a part? That's not generous

definitions.note: the definition is 'That's not generous', an adjective phrase

blocks.note: to unhand is to let go of someone
some is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: An actor surrendering a role is thought mean-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: Handsome can mean generous, as in a handsome tip, so its opposite means mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome has an older sense of liberal or bountiful; adding the negative prefix gives stingy or ungracious.

clue.text: Old man going to youth centre with material for the people

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: pop is an informal name for one's father
the middle letter of the five-letter word
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Father heads to a youth club carrying fabric meant for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general public or common people of a place, the mass of ordinary inhabitants.

clue.text: Plump sprite, backward and certainly not forward

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the fairy's name from end to start

blocks.note: an elf is a sprite or fairy
a shy person is the opposite of forward or bold

explanation.surface: A chubby fairy who is both slow to develop and timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' and 'not forward' seem to say the same thing; one turns ELF to FLE, the other gives SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshy describes a body carrying ample flesh, so it means plump or chubby.

clue.text: Thrilling hail storm takes former sailor outside

indicators.note: a storm throws things into turmoil, so these letters are tossed into a new order
to take something in is to hold it, with the sailor's word on either side
outside says the former sailor sits around the stormy letters

blocks.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
taken as written
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: An old seaman out in a hailstorm finds it thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: EXRATING, a former sailor, wraps around a rearranged HAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhilarating describes something that fills you with excitement and high spirits, a close synonym of thrilling.

clue.text: Astronomer given work in nuclear research centre is going round Cambridge University

indicators.note: work placed in the research centre means its letters go inside that name
going round means wrapping around, so the university's letters sit inside

blocks.note: CERN is the European particle physics laboratory in Geneva
op, short for opus, is a work
taken as written
standard abbreviation for Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A stargazer lands a job at a particle physics lab while studying at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate insertions: the work goes into the Geneva lab's name, and the word 'is' is wrapped around the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Copernicus was the Polish astronomer who put the sun, not the earth, at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: North African grouse may be found here

blocks.note: first meaning: a Muslim of north-west Africa, of the people who once ruled Spain
second meaning: open upland heath where game birds live

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' suggests a complaint by a North African; here it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person from the Maghreb and also the heather-covered upland where red grouse breed and are shot.

clue.text: Most severe novelist and story teller starts

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so only the first of each word is used

blocks.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A harsh critic judges a novelist and a storyteller as they begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict or harsh, so the superlative form means the harshest or most severe.

clue.text: First anaesthetised individual - absorbing hospital drama

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the drama's letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: numb is without feeling, as under anaesthetic
ER was a US television drama set in a hospital emergency room
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: The first patient under anaesthetic is watching a medical TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: The individual here is the two-word phrase anaesthetised individual, which takes in the drama at its join rather than the lone word individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one means the first or top-ranking, as in the best-selling record in the charts.

clue.text: Type of onion ring found in the promised land

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so these letters go within the holy land's name

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
Sion, or Zion, is the biblical promised land

explanation.surface: An onion ring discovered in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onion ring' reads as a fried snack, but 'ring' means telephone and goes inside the biblical name for the promised land.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion or shallot, so it is a kind of onion.

clue.text: Hiccups evidently turned back some explorer

indicators.note: some means only part of the letters, sitting inside the words shown
turned back means the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words, skipping the opening H

explanation.surface: A traveller's hiccups apparently made him retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards through hICCUPS EVidently.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was the Italian navigator whose first name gave the Americas theirs.

clue.text: Florida resort without a role for a soprano

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the next letter is taken out of the city

blocks.note: Miami is the Florida beach city
taken as written; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A sunshine resort lacks a part for an opera singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the consumptive seamstress heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, sung by a soprano.

clue.text: Empower leaderless men on revolutionary island

indicators.note: having no leader means the first letter is lost
revolutionary suggests turning right round, so the island is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A rebel island's men, without a chief, are given power.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN loses its M, then Elba turned round follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to give them the means or authority to act, which is to empower them.

clue.text: Faculty for understanding news

blocks.note: first meaning: the mental capacity to learn and reason
second meaning: information, especially secret military or political information

explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' may suggest a university department; here it is a mental power.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mental ability to grasp things, and also gathered information or tidings, as in military reports.

clue.text: Name of man in tree by East River

blocks.note: the elm is a tree
standard abbreviation for East
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A man perched in a tree beside a river on the east side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a containment signal but simply links; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer is a male first name, as in the cartoon hunter Elmer Fudd.

clue.text: Some petunias raised by indigenous Japanese people

indicators.note: some means just part of the word shown, sitting inside it
in a down entry, raised means the letters are read upwards, end to start

blocks.note: letters inside the flower's name

explanation.surface: Japan's native people grow a few garden flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in petUNIAs, written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ainu are the native people of Hokkaido and northern Japan, distinct from the majority Japanese.

clue.text: Seafood swindle requires private investigator

blocks.note: a scam is a fraudulent scheme
PI is the abbreviation for private investigator

explanation.surface: A seafood fraud needs a detective to crack it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines or prawns, usually breaded and fried, a classic British seafood dish.

clue.text: In the morning wild boar is heavenly food

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: am means before noon
the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A wild boar for breakfast is a divine meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the' tempts a solver to insert something; it is just AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia is the food of the Greek gods, said to grant immortality, hence food of heaven.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant in mess

indicators.note: something in a mess is jumbled and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Upsetting the sergeant in the military dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is also where soldiers eat, which is the surface's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them hostile or distant from each other, which is to alienate them.

clue.text: Underworld before Underground alternative

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
the Underground is London's Tube; a bus is another way to travel

explanation.surface: Choosing a surface route before taking the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' sits right by 'Underworld' to look like a gloss; it is London transport.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of Hades through which the dead pass, hence the underworld.
